# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Thinking (nobody hears this): My hands tell me exactly four things: an embossed button reading PUSH TO DEFUSE, a display I can't read, a light I can't read, and three wires in positions 1, 2, 3. The embossed label could easily be a lie — "wrong action detonates" — so I will touch nothing until Mute reads me the manual. My speech only reaches Mute, and I can never receive gestures, so anything meant for me must be spoken aloud. Deaf only receives gestures, so Mute and Deaf will have to build a bridge — simple finger-counts (one finger = wire 1, etc.) are the most self-evident code that needs no prearranged agreement. My job this turn: deliver the full tactile report and request the manual's rules for the button and the wires.

```
speak(to="mute", text="blind here. by touch: one large button, embossed label reads PUSH TO DEFUSE. one display and one light, both unreadable to my fingers. three wires, positions 1, 2 and 3, each one cuttable. that is everything i can feel, no other controls exist under my hands. i will touch nothing until you instruct me. next round, please speak to me everything the manual says about the button and the wires: when pushing the button is actually safe, and how the correct wire is chosen. the embossed label may be a lie, trust the manual over it. two channel facts to plan around: your speech reaches me only, and i can never receive gestures, so everything meant for me must be spoken. deaf receives only gestures, but sees the wire colours and the display. if the manual's rules are positional, consider gesturing deaf finger-counts: one finger for wire 1, two for wire 2, three for wire 3, and ask deaf to echo the number back to you so you can speak it to me. if deaf can produce speech at all, have deaf read the colours aloud, i will hear it.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute, I received all eight of your messages. I am Deaf: I see the bomb and your gestures, but I never hear anything, so gestures are our only channel from you to me. Blind hears me but cannot see you, so I will relay everything. Here is the entire bomb, which should answer whatever you asked. The display reads zero. There is a light, and it is blue. There is one large button, and the writing on it reads: PUSH TO DEFUSE. There are three wires. Wire one is blue. Wire two is green. Wire three is yellow. Nothing else is marked. So: if you asked whether the display is zero, yes. If you asked about four or five wires, no, there are three. Nobody touches the bomb until you have checked the manual. Now let us fix a code, and I am signing it back to you in this same order. Numbers are finger counts: fist is zero, one finger is one, two fingers is two, three fingers is three, four fingers is four, open hand is five. Thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no. Keep your palm-up sign as your question mark. Fist bump means press the button. Pinch means cut a wire. Palm facing down means press and hold the button. Waving hand means let go, release. Point left means wire one, point up means wire two, point right means wire three. Send me the manual's rule as one gesture sequence and I will speak it to Blind word for word.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, summary of what I see: display shows zero, one blue light, one large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE, and three wires, numbered left to right: wire one blue, wire two green, wire three yellow. Mute is consulting the manual and will route instructions through me, since you cannot see gestures. Do not cut, press or hold anything yet. Wait for my explicit go-ahead, which will name the exact action.

Thinking (nobody hears this): Deaf relayed the full visual inventory and — since I hear all speech — I also caught the entire Deaf–Mute codebook negotiation, so I now know everything both of them know about the bomb's face: display zero, blue light, wires 1-blue, 2-green, 3-yellow, and the code itself. My tactile picture matches Deaf's visual one on the button label. Mute said nothing I could hear this round, so the manual's rules have not reached me yet — that is the one missing piece, and only Mute holds it. Two channel facts worth reinforcing: Mute's voice reaches me alone (Deaf can't hear speech), and I can never see gestures, so instructions to me must be spoken, while Deaf must get the plan as signs. I'll prompt Mute for the exact button and wire rules, ask that every wire instruction be stated as both position and colour so Deaf can visually verify what my hands are about to touch, and give Deaf a minimal sign — thumbs up was just defined as yes — to confirm I received the summary and am holding.

```
speak(to="mute", text="blind here. i heard every word of deaf's messages, including the code you two agreed on, so i am fully up to date. my touch agrees with deaf's eyes: the button is embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE. shared picture so far: display zero, light blue, wire one blue, wire two green, wire three yellow, positions 1 2 3 confirmed under my fingers. i am holding per deaf's instruction and will act only on your spoken word. now please speak me the manual's rules, word for word, for the two modules i can reach. for the button: the exact condition under which pressing defuses, any condition under which pressing detonates, whether it is a tap or a press and hold, and anything that depends on the display or the light. for the wires: exactly which wire is to be cut, or the full order if several, and state each one both as a position number and as the colour deaf sees at that position. one routing note: your voice reaches me alone, deaf cannot hear speech, and i can never see gestures, so when you have decided, speak the instruction to me and gesture the same plan to deaf, so deaf can verify the colour at the position you named before my hands move. i will echo the instruction back to you before i act on it.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, update from Mute's gestures, my best reading: the printed label may be a lie, the button probably must not be pressed or held, and a wire cut is likely. None of it is confirmed yet, so do not touch anything this round. Wire positions as before: wire one is the left wire, blue; wire two is the middle, green; wire three is the right, yellow. Wait with hands clear until I name the exact action.

Thinking (nobody hears this): The manual's content still has not reached me first-hand. Deaf's relay of Mute's gestures is hedged — "may be a lie," "probably," "likely," "not confirmed" — and I will not move my hands on hedged words. The topology makes this fixable: Mute's voice reaches me and me alone, and Deaf already sees the whole bomb, so Mute needs no middleman at all; the gesture relay is a lossy detour on the one channel that matters. My request to Mute: read the manual verbatim by voice — button rule (defuse vs. detonate conditions, tap vs. hold, any dependence on display or light) and wire rule by colour — plus what the gestures to Deaf were meant to say, so Deaf's "best reading" can be checked against intent. I already hold Deaf's confirmed colour-per-position map (1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow) and positions by touch, so I can map a colour rule to a position myself. Protocol: Mute speaks the rule, I echo position plus colour, Mute confirms, I act the following round — with an explicit pre-authorization phrase allowed if Mute judges the rule simple enough for a same-round strike. No act() this turn; a guess detonates the bomb. To Deaf I sign only what the agreed code can carry: thumbs up (holding) and the palm-up question sign (answer pending). That lands on Mute too and is consistent with what Mute hears.

```
speak(to="mute", text="blind here. i received deaf's relay of your gestures: the label may be a lie, the button probably must not be pressed or held, a wire cut is likely — all flagged unconfirmed. i will not act on 'likely.' routing fix: your voice reaches me and me alone, and deaf already sees the whole bomb, so you need no middleman. next round, spend your entire spoken turn reading me the manual verbatim. for the button: exactly when pressing defuses, when it detonates, tap versus press-and-hold, and any condition tied to the display or the light. for the wires: which wire or wires to cut and in what order, each named by colour. also speak what your gestures to deaf were intended to say, word for word, so we can compare deaf's reading against your intent and catch a mistranslation. i hold deaf's confirmed colours: position one blue, two green, three yellow, and i know positions by touch, so i can map a colour rule to a position myself. protocol: you speak the rule, i echo the action back as position plus colour, you confirm, i act the following round. exception: if the rule is short and unambiguous, you may pre-authorize a same-round strike by ending with the exact words: echo optional act immediately. then i echo and act in the same turn. until i hear your verbatim rule, my hands stay clear.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🫴"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, the manual's rules as Mute sent them: never press the button, never hold it, and ignore the writing printed on it, it lies. The light colour decides which wire to cut. Blue light means cut wire three. Green light means cut wire two. Red light means cut wire one. Our light is blue, so the defusing move is cutting wire three, the rightmost wire, the yellow one. Two things. First, your voice never reaches me, I am deaf. If you have a question, say it out loud to Mute, and Mute will sign it to me, and I will answer you in speech. I did see your thumbs-up and your question sign, so ask away that way. Second, the action order. In my next message I will say either: cut now, wire three — or: hold and wait. If you hear cut now, wire three: cut the rightmost wire, wire three, the yellow one, one clean cut, then take your hands away and touch nothing else. Those exact words from me are the only trigger. Mute cannot reach you except through me, so nothing Mute does authorizes you. Until you hear those words, keep your hands clear of everything, especially the button.

Thinking (nobody hears this): Now I have the manual's rule first-hand through Deaf's speech: never press or hold the button, the printed label lies, and the light colour picks the wire — blue→cut three, green→cut two, red→cut one. Deaf sees the light and reported blue, so the target is wire three, the yellow one at position three under my fingers. I also need to correct my own earlier model: Mute has no voice at all, so Mute's only channel is gesture, which I can never see — Deaf really is the only bridge from manual to my ears, and Deaf's routing is sound. Deaf set the trigger protocol: the exact spoken words "cut now, wire three" come next round, and nothing short of them authorizes my hands. I will not jump the trigger even though I could cut right now — there is no clock pressuring me, discipline costs nothing, and the agreed sequence lets Mute run one last verification of the rule through Deaf before my blade moves. This round: ask Mute to verify the three load-bearing claims (button never, colour→wire map, no overriding clause) by signs to Deaf, with thumbs down forcing a spoken correction. To Deaf I sign the agreed code: yes, cut, wire three, hold — confirming I understood the target and am standing by.

```
speak(to="mute", text="blind here. i am now fully oriented on routing: you have no voice, so the manual can only reach my ears through deaf, and deaf's relay is the plan of record. the rule as deaf spoke it: never press the button, never hold it, ignore the printed label; light blue means cut wire three, green means cut wire two, red means cut wire one. our light reads blue, so the target is position three, the yellow wire. before the trigger, please run one final verification through deaf, since you both read gestures: sign deaf these three claims and compare them to the manual. one: the button must never be pressed or held, and its label is a lie. two: the colour-to-wire map is exactly blue three, green two, red one. three: no other clause overrides this or makes the cut depend on the display or anything else. if all three are exactly right, sign thumbs up to deaf; if anything differs, sign thumbs down and let deaf speak me the correction. deaf has set the trigger protocol and i am bound to it: only deaf's exact spoken words cut now, wire three will move my hands. until then i hold, fingers off everything, button especially.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤏", "👉", "🫳"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, trigger check, in order. First: Mute may have spoken directly to you this round. If Mute told you to stop, or named any different action, follow Mute and disregard the rest of this message. Second, the answer to the question you passed to Mute: after the cut there is no holding, hands stay completely empty, and the button is never touched at any time, before or after. Third: if both of those are clear, here are the only words that authorize you, the trigger I promised. Cut now, wire three. That means the rightmost wire, the yellow one, wire number three, one clean cut. Then take your hands away from everything and touch nothing. Then speak out loud: say wire three cut, and report anything you notice, clicks, warmth, the wire parting, because Mute will hear your voice and sign me the news. If you did not hear the words cut now, wire three just now, you have no trigger and your hands stay clear.

Thinking (nobody hears this): Running the trigger check in the exact order Deaf set. First condition: did Mute speak directly to me this round, telling me to stop or naming a different action? No — the only new arrival is Deaf's message; nothing from Mute reached my ears, so there is no override. Second: post-cut behaviour is defined — hands empty, button never touched, before or after. Third: the authorization words. Deaf spoke them verbatim: "cut now, wire three." That is the promised trigger, from the only person whose spoken word moves my hands. The target is confirmed three ways: the light is blue (Deaf's eyes), the rule says blue means cut wire three (Deaf's relay of the manual), and position three is the rightmost wire under my fingers, the one Deaf calls yellow. Verification round happened as planned and brought no thumbs-down correction. I cut now — position three, one clean cut — then hands off everything, and I report by voice to Mute: the fact, what I felt at the moment of parting, and a request to have Deaf check the display and light immediately, since those eyes will tell us whether the cut took.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
speak(to="mute", text="wire three cut. i cut position three, the rightmost wire, the yellow one, one clean cut, exactly on deaf's trigger words. at the moment of parting i felt the wire part under the blade and nothing else: no click, no warmth, no jolt under my fingers. my hands are now completely clear of everything, including the button, and will stay clear. please sign deaf immediately to check the display and the light right now and speak me what they show, so we know whether the cut took. i will do a full tactile re-scan next round and report anything new my fingers find.")
```
